title: Enough points from a cover by finitary slices
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] in the fixed universe convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $(U_i)_{i\in I}$ be a set-indexed family of objects such that the coproduct of the associated sheaves of their representable presheaves $\coprod_{i\in I}h_{U_i}\to 1$ is an epimorphism in $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$. Here $h_U$ denotes the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(-,U)$, without any subcanonicity assumption. Assume that for every $i$, the slice site $\mathcal C/U_i$ with its localized topology [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] has finite limits and every covering family in it admits a finite covering refinement. Then $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ has a set-indexed family of points $p_j:\mathbf{Set}\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ whose inverse-image functors jointly reflect isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 00YN, lemma-criterion-points: a cover of the final object by objects whose slices satisfy Proposition 00YQ

proof.text: Fix $i\in I$ and give $\mathcal C/U_i$ the localized topology [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]; it is a small site in the size convention [def-weil-size-convention], its underlying category has finite limits and every covering family admits a finite covering refinement by hypothesis. These are exactly the hypotheses of [lem-trf-finitary-site-enough-points], which therefore gives a set $Q_i$ and points $q:\mathbf{Set}\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C/U_i)$, $q\in Q_i$, whose inverse images jointly reflect isomorphisms. The forgetful functor $j_i:\mathcal C/U_i\to\mathcal C$, $(V\to U_i)\mapsto V$, is continuous [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](3): a covering of $\mathcal C/U_i$ is by definition a covering of $\mathcal C$, and for $T\to V$ and a covering $\{V_k\to V\}$ over $U_i$ the fibre product $T\times_VV_k$ formed in $\mathcal C$ (it exists by site axiom (iii)) lies over $U_i$ and is the fibre product in $\mathcal C/U_i$, so $j_i$ preserves it. It is cocontinuous [def-weil-pbc-special-cocontinuous-functor](1): a covering $\{V_k\to V\}$ of $j_i(V\to U_i)=V$ in $\mathcal C$ is, with the composites $V_k\to V\to U_i$, a covering of $V/U_i$ in $\mathcal C/U_i$ whose image is the given family. By [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-cocontinuous-topos-adjunction], restriction $L_i\mathcal F=\mathcal F|_{U_i}$, $\mathcal F|_{U_i}(V/U_i)=\mathcal F(V)$, is the inverse image of a morphism of topoi $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C/U_i)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$: it preserves finite limits and has a right adjoint. By the composition clause of [def-trf-geometric-morphism], for every $q\in Q_i$ the composite $p_{i,q}:\mathbf{Set}\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ is a point of $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ with inverse image $p_{i,q}^{-1}=q^{-1}\circ L_i$, $\mathcal F\mapsto q^{-1}(\mathcal F|_{U_i})$. (This is the procedure of Stacks Lemma 05V1 (lemma-point-morphism-sites) cited in the source proof.)

proof.text: Let $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ be a morphism of sheaves of sets on $\mathcal C$ such that $p_{i,q}^{-1}(\varphi)$ is a bijection for all $i\in I$ and $q\in Q_i$. Fix $i$. By Step 1, $q^{-1}(\varphi|_{U_i})=p_{i,q}^{-1}(\varphi)$ is a bijection for every $q\in Q_i$, so the conservativity conclusion of [lem-trf-finitary-site-enough-points] for the family $Q_i$ shows that $\varphi|_{U_i}:\mathcal F|_{U_i}\to\mathcal G|_{U_i}$ is an isomorphism of sheaves on $\mathcal C/U_i$. Since $(\varphi|_{U_i})_{V/U_i}=\varphi_V$, this says: $\varphi_V:\mathcal F(V)\to\mathcal G(V)$ is bijective for every object $V$ of $\mathcal C$ that admits a morphism $V\to U_i$ for some $i$.

source.place: Lemma 0DW0 (lemma-criterion-points), proof: 'it suffices to show: if phi is a map of sheaves such that phi restricted to C/U_i is an isomorphism for all i, then phi is an isomorphism'.

proof.text: Let $P$ be the presheaf $W\mapsto\coprod_{i\in I}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(W,U_i)$ (disjoint union of sets). Its sheafification $P^\#$ [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] is the coproduct $\coprod_ih_{U_i}$ in $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$: for a sheaf $\mathcal H$, $\operatorname{Hom}(P^\#,\mathcal H)=\operatorname{Hom}(P,\mathcal H)=\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}(\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(-,U_i),\mathcal H)=\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}(h_{U_i},\mathcal H)$ by the universal property of sheafification, used twice. The terminal sheaf is $1(W)=\{*\}$. Fix an object $W$. Since $P^\#\to1$ is an epimorphism, [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-epi-locally-surjective] gives a covering $\{W_a\to W\}$ with sections of $P^\#$ over each $W_a$; by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] each such section is, on a covering $\{W_{ab}\to W_a\}$, the image of an element of $P(W_{ab})$, i.e. of a morphism $W_{ab}\to U_{i(a,b)}$. By site axiom (ii) of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], $\{W_k\to W\}_k:=\{W_{ab}\to W\}_{a,b}$ is a covering in which every $W_k$ maps to some $U_i$; so $\varphi_{W_k}$ is bijective by Step 2. Injectivity of $\varphi_W$: if $\varphi_W(s)=\varphi_W(s')$ then $s|_{W_k}=s'|_{W_k}$ for all $k$ by injectivity of $\varphi_{W_k}$, so $s=s'$ by the sheaf equalizer condition for $\mathcal F$. This holds for every object $W$. Surjectivity: for $t\in\mathcal G(W)$ choose $s_k\in\mathcal F(W_k)$ with $\varphi(s_k)=t|_{W_k}$. On $W_k\times_WW_l$ (it exists by site axiom (iii)) the two restrictions of $s_k,s_l$ both map to the restriction of $t$; as $\varphi_{W_k\times_WW_l}$ is injective by the previous sentence, they agree. The sheaf condition for $\mathcal F$ glues them to $s\in\mathcal F(W)$, and $\varphi(s)$ and $t$ agree on every $W_k$, hence $\varphi(s)=t$ by the sheaf condition for $\mathcal G$. Thus every $\varphi_W$ is bijective, and the sectionwise inverses form a natural inverse, so $\varphi$ is an isomorphism. (If $I=\emptyset$ the hypothesis forces every object to be covered by the empty family, every sheaf is terminal and the argument holds vacuously.)

source.place: Lemma 0DW0 (lemma-criterion-points), last part of the proof: by assumption (1) every W has a covering by W_j mapping to some U_i; bijectivity on W_j and W_j x_W W_j' and the sheaf condition.

proof.text: The family $\{p_{i,q}\}_{i\in I,\,q\in Q_i}$ is indexed by the set $\coprod_{i\in I}Q_i$, a set in the fixed universe [def-weil-size-convention] since $I$ and every $Q_i$ are sets. Steps 1--3 show that these points jointly reflect isomorphisms, which is the asserted conclusion.

split_report.summary: Split the finite-cover slice criterion into four steps. For each slice, apply the existing finite-cover enough-points theorem and transport its points through the localized-site/sheaf-slice equivalence; then use the assumed epimorphic coproduct of representables to descend local isomorphisms to the whole sheaf topos. No new nodes were needed because all non-elementary inputs already exist in the DAG.
split_report.blueprint: The steps realize the auxiliary enough-points criterion used by the current module-factorization route; the imported blueprint contains no separate enough-points paragraph, so the proof follows Stacks Tag 00YN explicitly.

tool_uses.why: Steps 1-2 apply Deligne's finite-cover criterion (Stacks 00YQ) to each slice as a black box; it is a general site-theoretic theorem filed in sec-trace-formula and no node of this unit states it.
Step 1 takes from it that restriction along the continuous cocontinuous forgetful functor C/U->C is the inverse image of a morphism of topoi; generic site lemma of sk-thm-properbasechange.
Step 3 uses that sections of a sheafification are locally sections of the presheaf; generic sheafification lemma of sk-thm-p1.
Step 3 uses that epimorphisms of sheaves of sets are locally surjective (Mathlib leaf).
